title: Basic Eligibility — Academic Cutoff (80th Percentile)
description: Students must have passed Class XII / equivalent examination above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their respective board examination in the academic year of application.
answer: To be eligible for CSSS, a student must have scored above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their respective board (e.g. CBSE, State Board) in the year they passed Class XII.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 4(i)

title: Family Income Ceiling — Rs. 8 Lakh Per Annum
description: The annual family income from all sources must not exceed Rs. 8 lakh (Rs. 8,00,000) per annum.
answer: The family income limit for CSSS is Rs. 8 lakh (Rs. 8,00,000) per year from all sources combined. Students whose family income exceeds this threshold are not eligible.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 4(ii)

title: Institutional Eligibility — Regular UGC-Recognized Course
description: Students must be enrolled in a regular degree course (not correspondence or distance mode) at a college or university recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) or other statutory bodies.
answer: The student must be studying in a regular (not distance/correspondence) undergraduate or postgraduate degree programme at a UGC-recognized college or university in India.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 4(iii)

title: Scholarship Amount — Technical and Professional Courses
description: For students pursuing technical/professional courses (e.g. Engineering, Medicine, Management), the scholarship amount is Rs. 20,000 per annum.
answer: Students in technical or professional courses (Engineering, Medicine, MBA, Architecture, etc.) receive Rs. 20,000 per year for the duration of their course (up to 5 years).
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 7(a)

title: Scholarship Amount — General Degree Courses
description: For students pursuing general degree courses (Arts, Commerce, Science), the scholarship amount is Rs. 10,000 per annum for the first three years.
answer: Students in general degree courses (BA, BSc, BCom, etc.) receive Rs. 10,000 per year for up to 3 years.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 7(b)

title: Annual Renewal — Minimum 50% Marks Required
description: To renew the scholarship each year, a student must secure at least 50% marks (or equivalent grade) in the previous year's annual examination.
answer: Annual renewal of CSSS requires a minimum of 50% marks (or equivalent CGPA) in the preceding year's examination. Failure to meet this threshold results in cancellation of the scholarship.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 9

title: Cannot Combine with Other Central Government Scholarships
description: CSSS cannot be availed simultaneously with any other Central Government scholarship. If selected for another Central Government scholarship, the student must choose one.
answer: A student cannot hold CSSS together with any other Central Government scholarship simultaneously. If awarded another central scholarship, the student must relinquish one.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 10

title: Change of College — NSP Notification Required
description: A scholar who changes college or university must inform the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and obtain fresh approval. The scholarship may continue if the new institution is UGC-recognized and the course is eligible.
answer: If a CSSS recipient changes their college or university, they must update their details on the National Scholarship Portal and get re-verified. The scholarship may continue if the new college is eligible.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 11

title: Application via National Scholarship Portal (NSP)
description: All applications for CSSS must be submitted through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at https://scholarships.gov.in/ within stipulated dates.
answer: Applications for CSSS are submitted exclusively online through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at https://scholarships.gov.in/. Physical applications are not accepted. Applications must be submitted before the deadline announced each year.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 5

title: Total Scholarships Available — 82,000 Per Year
description: Approximately 82,000 fresh scholarships are awarded each year under CSSS — 41,000 for boys and 41,000 for girls.
answer: CSSS awards approximately 82,000 scholarships per year — 41,000 to boys and 41,000 to girls — distributed across all states and UTs proportional to Class XII pass population.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 2

title: State-wise Quota — Proportional to Class XII Pass-outs
description: Scholarships are distributed among states and UTs in proportion to the number of students passing Class XII from each state/UT.
answer: The 82,000 slots are distributed across states and Union Territories proportionally based on the number of Class XII pass-outs from each state/UT board.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 2

title: Termination for False or Misleading Information
description: If a student is found to have provided false or misleading information in the application, the scholarship will be terminated immediately and the disbursed amount must be refunded.
answer: Providing false or misleading information leads to immediate termination of the scholarship. The student is required to refund all scholarship amounts already received.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 12

title: Disbursement via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)
description: Scholarship amounts are disbursed directly to the student's bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) via the PFMS system, linked to Aadhaar.
answer: CSSS scholarship money is transferred directly to the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). No cash or cheque payments are made.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 8

title: No Caste-Based Reservation — Merit-Only Scheme
description: CSSS is a merit-based scholarship. Caste-based reservation (SC/ST/OBC) does not apply to this scheme.
answer: CSSS is purely merit-based. There is no caste-based reservation under this scheme. Selection is based solely on Class XII board performance relative to other applicants in the same state.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 3

title: Scholarship Duration — Full Course Length
description: The scholarship is tenable for the full duration of the undergraduate or postgraduate course, subject to annual renewal.
answer: CSSS is awarded for the full duration of the degree course — 3 years for general degrees, up to 5 years for professional/technical courses — provided the student meets the annual renewal criteria each year.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 7

title: 5% PwD Reservation Within Gender Quota
description: Within the gender-wise quota (41,000 boys, 41,000 girls), 5% of slots are reserved for Persons with Disabilities (PwD).
answer: 5% of CSSS slots within each gender quota are reserved for Persons with Disabilities (PwD). PwD students still need to meet the academic and income eligibility criteria.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 2

title: Change of Stream — NSP Notification and Re-verification
description: If a student changes their stream of study (e.g. from Science to Commerce), they must inform NSP. Continuation is subject to verification that the new course is eligible under CSSS.
answer: Changing your stream (e.g. Science to Arts) requires notifying NSP and re-verification. The scholarship may continue only if the new course qualifies under the CSSS eligible courses list.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 11

title: Gap Year — Scholarship Suspended, Not Retroactive
description: If a student takes a gap year or interrupts their studies, the scholarship is suspended for that period and cannot be claimed retroactively.
answer: If a student takes a break from studies (gap year), CSSS is suspended during the break period. The scholarship cannot be claimed for the gap year retroactively.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 9

title: Income Certificate from Competent Authority Required
description: Applicants must upload a family income certificate issued by a competent authority (e.g. Tehsildar, SDM) as part of the NSP application.
answer: A family income certificate issued by a competent government authority (Tehsildar, SDM, or equivalent) must be uploaded on NSP during application. Self-declaration alone is not sufficient.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 5

title: Indian Nationality and School in India Required
description: Students must have passed their Class XII examination from a school in India and must be Indian nationals.
answer: CSSS is available only to Indian nationals who have passed Class XII from a school located in India. Students who passed from schools abroad are not eligible.
source: CSSS Official Guidelines, Ministry of Education, Clause 4
